title: Artinian infinitesimal lifting criterion for smoothness at a point
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $S$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $x\in X$. A *small extension* is a surjective ring homomorphism $\varphi:B'\to B$ of Artinian local rings whose kernel $I=\ker\varphi$ has length $1$ as a $B'$-module (so $I\cong B'/\mathfrak m_{B'}$, $\mathfrak m_{B'}I=0$ and $I^2=0$); write $i=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}B'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The following are equivalent:

(1) $f$ is smooth at $x$: there is an open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ with $x\in U$ such that $f|_U:U\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms];

(2) for every small extension $\varphi:B'\to B$ and every pair of morphisms of schemes $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$, $\beta:\operatorname{Spec}B'\to S$ with $f\circ\alpha=\beta\circ i$ and $\alpha$ mapping the closed (unique) point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ to $x$, there is a morphism $\gamma:\operatorname{Spec}B'\to X$ with $\gamma\circ i=\alpha$ and $f\circ\gamma=\beta$.

(This is Stacks 02HX, (1)$\Leftrightarrow$(3). Stacks defines smoothness at $x$ by an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\ni x$ over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R\to A$ a smooth ring map, Morphisms Definition 01V5; this is equivalent to (1) because smoothness is local on the source, Morphisms Lemma 01V6, and the smooth morphisms of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] are those of Morphisms Section 01V4 by More on Morphisms Lemma 02H6.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02HX (label lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point, line 3575), equivalence (1)<=>(3); small extension: algebra.tex Definition 02HS (definition-small-extension, line 38937); the proof reduces to affines and cites Algebra Lemma 02HT (lemma-smooth-test-artinian)

proof.text:
(Affine neighbourhoods.) As $S$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], it has an affine open cover by opens with Noetherian rings of sections; choose a member $V
i f(x)$ and put $R=\mathcal O_S(V)$, a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. As $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], the open $f^{-1}(V)
i x$ is covered by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ a finitely generated $R$-algebra; choose one, $U
i x$, and put $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$. Then $f(U)\subseteq V$; let $j_U:U	o X$, $j_V:V	o S$ be the inclusions and $f_{U,V}:U	o V$ the unique morphism with $j_V\circ f_{U,V}=f\circ j_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. Fix isomorphisms $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$, $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-pc-scheme]; under them $f_{U,V}$ is $\pi=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi_0$ for a unique ring map $\varphi_0:R	o A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the one making $A$ a finitely generated $R$-algebra, and $x$ is a prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02HX (lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point, line 3575), proof (reduction to affines, then Algebra Lemma 02HT)

proof.text: (Test diagrams at $x$ are diagrams of rings.) Let $\varphi:B'\to B$ be a small extension and $i=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-unique-prime] $\operatorname{Spec}B=\{\mathfrak m_B\}$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B'=\{\mathfrak m_{B'}\}$, and $i(\mathfrak m_B)=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_{B'}$. Let $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$, $\beta:\operatorname{Spec}B'\to S$ with $f\circ\alpha=\beta\circ i$ and $\alpha(\mathfrak m_B)=x$. Then $\alpha(\operatorname{Spec}B)=\{x\}\subseteq U$ and $\beta(\operatorname{Spec}B')=\{\beta(i(\mathfrak m_B))\}=\{f(x)\}\subseteq V$, so $\alpha=j_U\circ\alpha_U$, $\beta=j_V\circ\beta_V$ for unique $\alpha_U,\beta_V$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], and via the isomorphisms of step 1, $\alpha_U=\operatorname{Spec}a$, $\beta_V=\operatorname{Spec}\rho$ for unique ring maps $a:A\to B$, $\rho:R\to B'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since $\operatorname{Spec}a$ sends a prime $P$ to $a^{-1}(P)$, $\alpha(\mathfrak m_B)=x$ means $a^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak q$. As $j_V$ is a monomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism], $f\circ\alpha=\beta\circ i$, i.e. $j_V\circ f_{U,V}\circ\alpha_U=j_V\circ\beta_V\circ i$, is equivalent to $f_{U,V}\circ\alpha_U=\beta_V\circ i$, i.e. $\operatorname{Spec}(a\circ\varphi_0)=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi\circ\rho)$, i.e. $a\circ\varphi_0=\varphi\circ\rho$ (functoriality and uniqueness in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]). Conversely, ring maps $a,\rho$ with $a\circ\varphi_0=\varphi\circ\rho$ and $a^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak q$ give the test pair $\alpha=j_U\circ\operatorname{Spec}a$, $\beta=j_V\circ\operatorname{Spec}\rho$ at $x$. So the test data of condition (2) for $f$ at $x$ correspond bijectively to the data $(\varphi,\rho,a)$ of condition (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-artinian-lifting] for $(R,\varphi_0,\mathfrak q)$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02HX (lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point, line 3575), proof (reduction to affines, then Algebra Lemma 02HT)

proof.text: (Lifts correspond.) In the situation of step 2, let $\gamma:\operatorname{Spec}B'\to X$ satisfy $\gamma\circ i=\alpha$. Its image is $\{\gamma(i(\mathfrak m_B))\}=\{x\}\subseteq U$, so $\gamma=j_U\circ\gamma_U$ with $\gamma_U=\operatorname{Spec}a'$ for a unique ring map $a':A\to B'$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since $j_U$ and $j_V$ are monomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism], $\gamma\circ i=\alpha$ iff $\gamma_U\circ i=\alpha_U$ iff $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi\circ a')=\operatorname{Spec}a$ iff $\varphi\circ a'=a$, and $f\circ\gamma=\beta$, i.e. $j_V\circ f_{U,V}\circ\gamma_U=j_V\circ\beta_V$, iff $\operatorname{Spec}(a'\circ\varphi_0)=\operatorname{Spec}\rho$ iff $a'\circ\varphi_0=\rho$. Conversely a ring map $a'$ with $\varphi\circ a'=a$ and $a'\circ\varphi_0=\rho$ gives $\gamma=j_U\circ\operatorname{Spec}a'$ with $\gamma\circ i=\alpha$ and $f\circ\gamma=\beta$. With step 2: condition (2) of this lemma for $f$ at $x$ holds iff condition (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-artinian-lifting] holds for $(R,\varphi_0,\mathfrak q)$.

proof.text:
(Smoothness at $x$ is smoothness at $\mathfrak q$.) Suppose (1): $U'
i x$ open with $f|_{U'}:U'	o S$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then $W_0=U\cap U'$ is open in $U'$ and in $U$, contains $x$, and $f|_{U'}(W_0)\subseteq V$; by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] (a) applied to $f|_{U'}$, the induced $W_0	o V$ is smooth, and by uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] it is the restriction of $f_{U,V}$ to $W_0$. Under $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$, $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$, $W_0$ corresponds to an open $W
i\mathfrak q$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $W_0	o V$ to $\pi|_W$, which is therefore smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] (c): condition (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-artinian-lifting] holds. Conversely, given an open $W
i\mathfrak q$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $\pi|_W$ smooth, let $W_0\subseteq U$ be the corresponding open; it is open in $X$ and contains $x$, the restriction $W_0	o V$ of $f_{U,V}$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] (c), and by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] (b) applied to $f$ with the opens $W_0\subseteq X$, $V\subseteq S$, $f|_{W_0}:W_0	o S$ is smooth. So (1) holds with the open $W_0$.

proof.text: (Conclusion.) $R$ is Noetherian and $\varphi_0$ makes $A$ a finitely generated $R$-algebra (step 1), so by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-artinian-lifting] its conditions (1) and (2) for $(R,\varphi_0,\mathfrak q)$ are equivalent. By step 4 condition (1) of this lemma is equivalent to the first, and by steps 2 and 3 condition (2) of this lemma is equivalent to the second; hence (1)$\Leftrightarrow$(2).
